_note: Hand-translated English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Shemot 2 (Moses' birth, killing of the Egyptian, flight to Midian, marriage to Zipporah). Saadia-distinctive moves: v.1 רגל מן אל לוי = 'a man of the family of Levi' (אל = family); v.3 תאבות מן ברדי = 'an ark of papyrus' (ברדי preserves Egyptian-derived term for גמא); v.3 וקפרתהא באלקפר ואלזפת = 'sealed it with bitumen and pitch'; v.3 אלדיס = 'the reed-thicket' (for סוף); v.3,5 שאטי/שאטה = 'the bank of' (Nile); v.5 לתג'סל פי אלניל = 'to bathe in the Nile' (Saadia takes על-היאר as 'in the Nile'); v.5 פמדת ידהא = 'and she stretched out her hand' (Saadia reads אמתה as 'her [own] forearm', not 'her maidservant' — interpretive move parallel to Rashi's first reading); v.6 אשפקת = 'had compassion'; v.7,9 מרצ'עה / ארצ'עי = 'nursing mother / nurse him'; v.10 נשלתה מן אלמא = 'I drew him out from the water' (etymological gloss on Moses' name); v.12 פאלתפת ימנה ויסרה = 'turned right and left' (Saadia smooths the Hebrew duplication כה וכה); v.13 לאלצ'אלם = 'to the unjust one' (for הרשע); v.14 רייסא וחאכמא = 'a chief and a judge' (for שר ושפט); v.14 איקינא קד ערף אלכ'בר = 'indeed, the matter has become known' (איקינא = the Saadia 'verily' particle); v.15 בלד מדין = 'the land of Midian'; v.15 בין ידיה = 'from before him' (the standard 'in his presence' idiom); v.16 לאמאם מדין = 'to the imām of Midian' (Saadia uses אמאם — 'leader/imām' — for כהן מדין, avoiding 'priest' which carries cultic implication); v.16 אלחיאץ' = 'the troughs'; v.21 אמען פי אלמקאם = 'consented to dwell'; v.22 צרת ג'ריבא פי בלד ג'רבה = 'I became a stranger in a strange land'; v.23 פתנהד = 'they groaned'; v.23 תג'וותהם = 'their plea'; v.24 שהיקהם = 'their groaning' (deep-sighing); v.25 ורחמהם = 'and had mercy on them' (Saadia expands וידע אלהים to 'beheld + had mercy' — rationalizing the divine 'knowing' as compassionate regard).

translations.1: Then a man of the family of Levi went, and married the daughter of Levi.
translations.2: And the woman conceived, and bore a son; and when she saw that he was fair, she hid him for three months.
translations.3: And she could no longer hide him; so she took for him an ark of papyrus, and sealed it with bitumen and pitch; and she set the babe inside it, and set it in the reed-thicket upon the bank of the Nile.
translations.4: And his sister stood at a distance, to see what would be done with him.
translations.5: And Pharaoh's daughter came down to bathe in the Nile; and her maids walked along its bank. She saw the ark in the midst of the reed-thicket, and she stretched out her hand and took it.
translations.6: And she opened it and saw him — behold, a babe was crying; and she had compassion on him, and said: 'This is one of the children of the Hebrews.'
translations.7: She said to her: 'Shall I go and call for you a nursing woman from the Hebrews, that she may nurse him for you?'
translations.8: Pharaoh's daughter said to her: 'Go.' And the maiden went, and called the mother of the babe.
translations.9: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: 'Here, take this babe — nurse him for me, and I will give you your wage.' And the woman took the babe, and nursed him.
translations.10: And when the babe grew, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter; and he became to her like a son. And she named him Moses, saying: 'For I drew him out from the water.'
translations.11: And it was in those days that Moses grew up, and he went out to his brothers, and he looked upon their burdens. And behold, an Egyptian man was striking a Hebrew man, one of his brothers.
translations.12: And he turned right and left, and saw that there was no one [about]; and he struck the Egyptian, and he died; and he buried him in the sand.
translations.13: And he went out on the second day; and behold, two Hebrew men were quarreling. And he said to the unjust one of them: 'Why do you strike your companion?'
translations.14: And he said: 'Who set you a chief and a judge over us? Do you intend to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?' And Moses was alarmed, and said: 'Indeed, the matter has become known.'
translations.15: And when Pharaoh heard of this matter, he sought to kill Moses. And Moses fled from before him, and came to the land of Midian, and sat by the well.
translations.16: And the imām of Midian had seven daughters; and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
translations.17: And the shepherds came and drove them away; and Moses arose and aided them, and watered their flock.
translations.18: And when they came to Reuel their father, he said: 'What is your concern that you have hurried to come today?'
translations.19: And they said to him: 'An Egyptian man rescued us from the hand of the shepherds; and he also drew water for us, and watered the flock.'
translations.20: He said to his daughters: 'And where is he? Why have you left the man? Call him, that he may eat a meal.'
translations.21: And Moses consented to dwell with the man; and he gave him Zipporah his daughter [in marriage].
translations.22: And she bore a son; and he named him Gershom — for he said: 'I became a stranger in a strange land.'
translations.23: And it was also in those long days that the king of Egypt died; and the sons of Israel groaned because of their hard service, and they cried out; and their plea ascended to God from the [hard] service.
translations.24: And God heard their groaning, and remembered His covenant, which was with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translations.25: And God beheld them, and had mercy on them.
